title: NBA raises salary cap projections for 2027-28, giving cap-strapped teams measure of relief
content:
The NBA recently informed teams of its updated salary cap projections for the 2027-28 season, league sources told The Athletic, with the new projections coming in $2 million higher than the league’s previous numbers.

Those sources, speaking on condition of anonymity because the projections have not been made public, said the league is now projecting the 2027-28 salary cap will rise to $176 million and the luxury tax line will be $213 million.

The news is sweet relief for teams facing salary cap and apron crunches, as much for the direction as the magnitude.

The latest national TV contract was supposed to usher in an era of 10 percent annual salary cap raises, more than enough to cover the 8 percent raises in contracts given to most star players. Instead, the local TV market crashed so hard that the annual raise was barely half that a year ago (5.2%) and was forecast to be similar in 2027-28 (5.5%). The projected raise for 2027-28 is now a healthier 6.7 percent — still a far cry from the maximal 10 percent, but closer to the raises in player contracts.

Additionally, the increased projections flip a recent trend of every cap update from the league shifting future estimates lower, thus making it even more challenging for teams to navigate the aprons in future seasons.

This will also be welcome news for players whose max-contract extensions are tied to the 2027-28 cap number, most notably Victor Wembanyama and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, and it increases the max salary for potential 2027 free agents such as Nikola Jokic and Jalen Duren.
